evidence: app/src/api.ts:35 — fetch, the most advanced data API used; stable for a decade
app/src/main.ts:27 — popstate/pushState client routing, stable since 2010s
app/src/components.ts:18 — loading="lazy" img attribute, Baseline-widely-available since 2022
app/server.mjs:2-6 — only node:http, node:fs, node:fs/promises, node:path, fileURLToPath; all long-stable
app/package.json:13-16 — devDeps vite ^8.3.5 and typescript ^5.9.3, both current stable releases (verified)
reach.rationale: Every API in the app — browser, Node, and build tool — is long-stable; the newest surface is Vite 8 itself (stable since 2026-03-12), and the app touches it through only its most basic, pre-existing config API.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:3-16 — the only framework-specific code is one 14-line dev-server middleware plugin, isolated in a single file
app/package.json:11-12 — build scripts depend only on vite build and node server.mjs; no runtime dependencies at all
app/src/style.css — no experimental CSS features to contain
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; even the framework touch-points (dev plugin, server) are each confined to one self-contained file with zero runtime library coupling.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:7-15 — the custom middleware exists only to serve /config.js in dev, mirroring app/server.mjs:33, which is required by the spec's runtime API_BASE_URL injection
app/src/api.ts:1-13 — runtime config read via a plain window global; no experimental module/import-meta mechanisms used
app/src/nav.ts:1-14 — a 14-line hand-rolled history wrapper instead of any routing library
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, so there is nothing gratuitous; where the app could have reached for new machinery (routing, hydration, signals) it used long-stable primitives.

findings.issue: Vite 8 is the first Rolldown-based major (stable 2026-03-12), so the build toolchain is younger than a typical LTS choice; a future minor could shift bundling behavior.
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is since it is the current stable release and the lockfile pins 8.3.5; the app uses only defineConfig + a configureServer hook, so a future downgrade to Vite 7 would also be trivial.

summary: The app rests entirely on long-stable browser, Node and CSS APIs with zero runtime dependencies and no experimental or preview surfaces. The newest element is the toolchain version itself — Vite 8 (stable March 2026) and TypeScript 5.9 — and even those are used only through their most basic, stable APIs. Experimental-API risk is effectively zero.
